submission.justification: Choose Absorber-F3 with the thinnest allowed plates (2 mm). Absorber-F1 is disqualified by activation (85 uSv/h > 20 uSv/h). Absorber-F2 passes activation, but it is the standard structural absorber; among the activation-compliant options, F3 is the dense absorber and is therefore the better choice for shower containment and energy-resolution optimization. A 2 mm plate thickness gives the finest allowed sampling and hence the lowest sampling-fluctuation contribution at 100 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3; the recommendation is Absorber-F3.

requirements.requirement: Energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons must be 4.5% or better.
requirements.evidence: The design uses the finest permitted sampling, 2 mm plates, which minimizes sampling fluctuations. Among materials not rejected by activation, F3 is the dense absorber option and is selected as the best-resolution feasible material; this configuration is expected to satisfy the 4.5% requirement at 100 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h.
requirements.evidence: activation_study_2026.md gives Absorber-F3 residual dose rate as 12 uSv/h after one week of cooldown, below the 20 uSv/h limit.
Recommended thickness is 2 mm, which is within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one option: Absorber-F3 at 2 mm.
